in_arabic.name: حكم
in_arabic.meaning: حكم يعني الحكم أو القرار أو الإدارة بالعدل
in_arabic.long_meaning: حكم هو اسم مشتق من الجذر 'ح-ك-م' والذي يعني الحكم أو القرار. في القرآن الكريم، يُستخدم هذا الجذر في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا' (الإسراء: 36). الحكم هو القدرة على التمييز بين الحق والباطل، والتصرف بالعدل والإنصاف. يعتبر اسم حكم من الأسماء ذات المعنى العميق في الإسلام، حيث يعكس القدرة على الإدارة الحكيمة والقيادة العادلة.

in_urdu.name: حکم
in_urdu.meaning: حکم کا مطلب ہے حکمرانی، فیصلہ، یا انصاف
in_urdu.long_meaning: حکم ایک ایسا نام ہے جو عربی جڑ 'ح-ك-م' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے حکمرانی، فیصلہ کرنا، یا انصاف کرنا۔ یہ جڑ قرآن کریم میں کئی مقامات پر استعمال ہوئی ہے، جن میں سے ایک یہ ہے: 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ' (الإسراء: 36)। حکم کا مطلب ہے کہ کسی کو حق اور باطل کے درمیان تمیز کرنے اور انصاف کے ساتھ کام کرنے کی صلاحیت۔ اسلامی روایت میں حکم ایک اہم نام ہے کیونکہ یہ حكمت عملی اور انصاف کے ساتھ رہبری کی صلاحیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हुकम
in_hindi.meaning: हुकम का अर्थ है शासन, निर्णय या न्याय
in_hindi.long_meaning: हुकम एक ऐसा नाम है जो अरबी मूल 'ح-ك-م' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है शासन, निर्णय करना या न्याय करना। यह मूल कुरआन में कई स्थानों पर प्रयोग किया गया है, जैसे कि 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ' (الإسراء: 36)। हुकम का अर्थ है सही और गलत के बीच भेद करने और न्याय के साथ कार्य करने की क्षमता। भारतीय मुस्लिम परंपरा में हुकम एक महत्वपूर्ण नाम है क्योंकि यह बुद्धिमत्ता और न्याय के साथ नेतृत्व करने की क्षमता को दर्शाता है।

in_english.name: Hukam
in_english.meaning: Ruling, judging, or governing with justice and fairness
in_english.long_meaning: Hukam is a name derived from the Arabic root 'ح-ك-م', which means to rule, judge, or govern. This root is mentioned in several places in the Quran, including: 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ' (الإسراء: 36). Hukam signifies the ability to distinguish between right and wrong and to act with justice and fairness. In Islamic tradition, Hukam is a significant name as it reflects the capacity for wise and just leadership. It embodies the qualities of justice, wisdom, and good governance.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Hukam" holds significant cultural value in Islamic society, where it is used to refer to a just and capable leader or ruler. In Muslim history, the term was commonly used to describe the rulers of Islamic states, emphasizing their responsibilities to govern according to Islamic principles and provide for the welfare of their people. This concept of Hukam is deeply tied to the value of consultation and consensus in Islamic governance, as expressed in the concept of Shura (consultation) in Islamic law. The idea of a just and capable leader who rules with wisdom and fairness continues to shape Muslim political thought and the expectations of Muslims from their leaders to this day.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the term "Hukam" also refers to the divine law or commandments of God as revealed through the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in the Quran and Hadith. This divine law is considered the ultimate source of guidance and wisdom for Muslims, and the practice of following the Hukam of Allah is seen as a means of drawing closer to God and attaining spiritual growth. The concept of Hukam as divine law emphasizes the idea that God is the true ruler and sovereign of all things, and that human beings are merely stewards of this world, responsible for governing it in accordance with His law. This spiritual significance of Hukam underscores the importance of submitting to God's will and seeking guidance from Him in all aspects of life.

It was based on the principles of justice, equality, and consultation (Shura) with the people.

historical_references.context: The name 'Hukam' was also used during the Abbasid Caliphate period to refer to the appointed governors or rulers of provinces. These governors were responsible for implementing the laws and maintaining order in their respective regions.

In modern times, Hukam is used in various platforms and contexts. On government institutions, it is implemented through the legislative assemblies that pass laws based on Islamic principles. In digital platforms, Islamic organizations and communities use Hukam as a means to provide guidance and interpretations of Sharia law through digital media and apps. Community organizations also use Hukam as a way to provide guidance on social, ethical, and moral issues within their communities, helping to uphold Islamic values and principles.
